target.title: Serve item attachments
target.description:
Customers asked to download item manuals and spec sheets.
Adds GET /attachments/{filename}, served from the attachments volume.

summary: Adds a new endpoint to serve item attachments from a directory based on a filename route parameter.

suspects.title: Path traversal vulnerability via filename parameter
suspects.problem: Using os.path.join with an untrusted filename parameter without sanitization allows an attacker to supply path traversal sequences (like ../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the filesystem accessible to the application process.
suspects.how_to_check: Verify whether os.path.commonpath or a similar check is used elsewhere in the repository to restrict file paths to ATTACHMENT_DIR, and check if filenames can contain directory separators.

suspects.title: Reading entire file into memory with handle.read()
suspects.problem: Reading the entire attachment file into memory using handle.read() can lead to high memory consumption or Out-Of-Memory errors if large manuals or spec sheets are downloaded concurrently.
suspects.how_to_check: Check the implementation of Response.file in app/web.py to see if it supports streaming or file-like objects rather than raw byte strings.

Category: security

Suspected problem: Using os.path.join with an untrusted filename parameter without sanitization allows an attacker to supply path traversal sequences (like ../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the filesystem accessible to the application process.
What would confirm or refute it: Verify whether os.path.commonpath or a similar check is used elsewhere in the repository to restrict file paths to ATTACHMENT_DIR, and check if filenames can contain directory separators.

The file at the traversed path is opened and returned.

arguments.explanation: The get_attachment endpoint takes a filename parameter from the route and joins it with ATTACHMENT_DIR using os.path.join. Because `filename` can contain directory traversal sequences (such as `../`), an attacker can supply sequences to escape ATTACHMENT_DIR and read arbitrary files accessible to the application process.
arguments.claim: Using os.path.join with an untrusted filename parameter without path traversal validation allows an attacker to read arbitrary files via directory traversal sequences.
arguments.suggested_fix: Resolve the absolute path using os.path.realpath or os.path.abspath and verify that it starts with ATTACHMENT_DIR (or use os.path.commonpath) before opening the file.

arguments.suggested_fix: Update Response or web framework to support streaming file responses or chunked iterables instead of reading entire files into byte strings.
arguments.explanation: In app/routes/attachments.py, the endpoint opens attachment files and reads their entire contents into memory via `handle.read()` to pass to `Response.file`. Looking at `Response.file` in app/web.py, it takes `data: bytes` and stores the whole byte string in `Response.body`. Consequently, large attachments (manuals, spec sheets) will be loaded fully into memory, leading to high memory usage and potential Out-Of-Memory errors under concurrent downloads.
